name: sort
algorithm: Each standard library's unstable sort of n u64 values: per round r the values are splitmix64 from seed + r * 0x5555555555555555, sorted ascending, and every 1,024th value times its index plus the last value is added to the checksum with wrapping (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; there is no checked arithmetic to remove

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, each with its own algorithm; the sorted order of distinct keys is unique, so the sampled checksum checks every column sorted
notes: Algorithms: Mk Slice.Sort is Go's pdqsort_func with ipnsort's branch-free cyclic Lomuto partition for elements of at most 32 bytes (std/core/core_sort.mk, D8-32), the comparator inlined; Rust slice::sort_unstable is ipnsort; Zig std.mem.sortUnstable is pdqsort; Go slices.Sort is pdqsort; C qsort is the C runtime's (UCRT on Windows), with an indirect comparison call per compare.

The same task and sources as core-new/sort (M7's row, Mk's Sort before the Lomuto partition); the quick size and checksum are core-new's, so the two rows compare the old and the new Sort there. The publish size is the contract's (plan/06-m6.md 4.1: std sort of 10 M u64), one round of n = 10,000,000, where core-new publishes ten rounds of 1,000,000 (SD8-X-10: 8 MB of keys fit the publish machine's 96 MB L3, 80 MB do not).
